# Use a standard Ubuntu 22.04 base image
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to avoid prompts during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers, Git, wget, ca-certificates, and OpenMPI
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# This allows running MPI applications as the root user, oversubscribing CPU cores,
# and disables a shared memory mechanism that can cause issues in containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set the source build directory
WORKDIR /usr/local/src

# --- Build and install hypre dependency ---
# Version 2.28.0 with fortran disabled and bigint enabled as required.
# FIX: Added --prefix=/usr/local to ensure hypre installs to a system-wide path
# that the subsequent mfem build can find.
RUN HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf hypre.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install

# --- Build and install metis dependency ---
# Version 4.0.3 from the specified URL with required OPTFLAGS.
# Metis-4 does not have a 'make install' target; it will be referenced by its build path.
RUN METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz -O metis.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf metis.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    make OPTFLAGS=-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration

# --- Build and install mfem dependency ---
# Version 4.7, built in parallel and linked against the local builds of hypre and metis.
RUN MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v${MFEM_VERSION} https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS_4=YES METIS_DIR=/usr/local/src/metis-4.0.3 HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local

# --- Build the laghos application ---
# Clone the repository and build against the local mfem build.
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local/src/mfem && \
    # Copy the final executable to a location on the system's PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/

# Set the final runtime working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the application data files from the build location to the runtime working directory
RUN cp -r /usr/local/src/Laghos/data .

# --- Final Cleanup ---
# Remove the source code and build artifacts to minimize final image size.
RUN rm -rf /usr/local/src

# Set the default command to run the application executable
CMD ["/usr/local/bin/laghos"]

#
# MiniCluster Manifest for a Laghos HPC experiment on AWS CPU instances
#
# This manifest defines a Flux MiniCluster to run the Laghos hydrodynamics
# proxy application. It is configured for a single-node execution.
#
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for our MiniCluster instance
  name: laghos-cpu-experiment
  # Deploy to the 'default' namespace as instructed
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to create for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the entire job on a single Kubernetes node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job. Flux will distribute these
  # tasks across the pods defined by 'size'. Here, all 4 tasks run on the single pod.
  tasks: 4

  # Logging verbosity and strictness for the Flux Operator
  logging:
    # Enforce strict schema validation for the CRD
    strict: true

  # Per instructions, do not delete pods after the job finishes.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

  # Specification for the application container. Only one is needed.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      # The command to run the Laghos application.
      # 'flux run' is prepended by the Flux Operator automatically.
      # This command runs Laghos with problem 1 (-p 1) using the specified mesh file.
      # The mesh file is assumed to be in a 'data' subdirectory relative to the working directory.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m data/cube_311_hex.mesh

      # As per specific instructions, launcher is explicitly false.
      # The Flux Operator will default to using the first container in the list
      # to launch the command, so this still functions as intended.
      launcher: false

      # No resource requests or limits are defined, allowing the container
      # to use the full CPU and memory of the node (Burstable QoS class).
